subject: Voss
fact: Voss is a former bandit who was coerced into service due to gambling debts, alcoholism, and the forced sale of his property; he is terrified of being executed by the Church of St. Cuthbert for alleged cult membership.
source_quote: The Moathouse was a good hideout because nobody wanted to come here anymore. The Temple was dead, and adventurers picked this place clean, so nobody came here.

subject: Calmer
fact: Calmer is a cleric of St. Cuthbert who takes grim pleasure in explaining the Church’s punitive doctrines, deliberately exacerbating Voss’s terror under the guise of 'calming' him.
source_quote: I think it’s important that we call to calm down.

subject: Sequoia
fact: Sequoia is a rogue who shows reluctant empathy toward Voss, rejecting execution in favor of interrogation, and is the first to notice and investigate the mysterious symbol.
source_quote: Look, I know you are just a desperate man caught up in something bigger than themselves. And I really don’t need to hand you over to the authorities. I just need to know what this symbol is.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr is a monk who uses illusion magic to manipulate enemies and is dismissive of Voss’s knowledge, believing him too low on the hierarchy to be useful.
source_quote: He’s too low down the totem pole to know anything useful.

subject: Zinia
fact: Zinia is a rogue who executes precise, silent takedowns and follows Sequoia’s lead in interrogation, showing no overt emotion but contributing to the group’s tactical cohesion.
source_quote: Keep him alive. We want to interrogate him.

subject: Church of St. Cuthbert
fact: The Church of St. Cuthbert enforces brutal penalties for suspected membership in rival cults, treating affiliation as a capital offense; its reputation for zealous punishment has instilled terror in the region.
source_quote: Membership in the cult is punishable by death.

subject: The Moathouse
fact: The Moathouse was once a religious site tied to a now-dead temple, later used as a bandit hideout after being thoroughly looted and abandoned by adventurers; it is now a scene of recent violence and death.
source_quote: The Moathouse was a good hideout because nobody wanted to come here anymore. The Temple was dead, and adventurers picked this place clean, so nobody came here.

subject: Flat river rock with eye and tear
fact: A small, inscribed river stone bearing the symbol of an eye and a tear; it was given by a higher authority to signify belonging to a hidden network, and its presence triggers extreme fear in Voss.
source_quote: It’s what the big boss gave the boss who gave it to us. It meant we belonged.

subject: Bandits
fact: A group of armed outlaws, formerly tied to the Moathouse’s ruined temple; most were killed in a surprise attack by the party, three escaped through an enlarged arrow slit, and one remains alive for interrogation.
source_quote: Three of the bandits escape to the south through an arrow slit that has been enlarged to allow easy retreat.

subject: Moathouse raid
fact: The party launched a coordinated, stealthy assault on the Moathouse, killing nine bandits and capturing one; the attack began with illusion-based door manipulation and ended with the group securing the site for interrogation.
source_quote: Zephyr has used an illusion to get the folks inside to open the door for us.

subject: The Eye and Tear Symbol
fact: The origin and meaning of the eye-and-tear symbol remain unknown; it is linked to a higher authority within a hidden network, possibly tied to the dead temple or a secret cult, and its presence suggests a deeper conspiracy.
source_quote: It’s what the big boss gave the boss who gave it to us. It meant we belonged.

subject: session date
fact: The events occur during a single session of play, marked by a sequence of combat, interrogation, and revelation, culminating in the discovery of the eye-and-tear symbol and the bandit’s emotional breakdown.
source_quote: Sequoia then wakes up the bandit.
